findings.title: Tailworm: Tailscale Flaws and Who Is Exposed - Brandefense
findings.summary_md: The Tailworm report published 24 October 2026 by Erica Windisch of Cyberdione Labs lists 11 findings in Tailscale client v1.104.2 and headscale v0.29.5, with six rated high severity. As of 26 October 2026 no patch is released, though Tailscale has unreleased commits addressing some findings.

findings.title: Tailworm report published on tailworm.com
findings.summary_md: Cyberdione Labs published the Tailworm audit report on 24 October 2026, documenting 11 verified flaws discovered during lab testing from 22-24 October on unmodified Tailscale v1.104.2 and headscale v0.29.5 software. The most critical finding allows authorized attackers to gain root via Unix-socket forwarding in Tailscale SSH.

findings.title: Unpatched Tailscale SSH Flaws Could Let a Hacked Device Reach Root on Other Servers - The Hacker News
findings.summary_md: The findings were published 25 October 2026 in the Tailworm report by Erica Windisch. Four findings target Tailscale SSH, which performs forwarding with root privileges and can be bypassed; a compromised device permitted to reach another over SSH can gain root and steal network-joining keys.
